key_driver_codes: Major Small and Large Bowel Procedures with CC

patterns_data.pattern_details: Acute hospital spend is rising across several Medicaid products because admissions are up and, in the largest markets, paid per admit is also higher. CA is the largest driver, but similar patterns repeat in MO, TN, OH, NC, IN, and MD, which makes this a recurring hospital economics and utilization issue rather than a one-off spike. The pattern is concentrated in bowel, liver, and behavioral health-related inpatient DRGs.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: This is a repeatable inpatient cost mechanism with both utilization and reimbursement exposure across multiple markets.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Run a joint UM and reimbursement review of acute hospital admissions, starting with CA and then MO and TN, focused on admission appropriateness, level of care, inpatient conversion, and hospital contract exposure for the listed DRGs.
evidence_summary: CA TANF Standard acute hospital spend rose +$1.9M, led by +37 admissions in Major Small and Large Bowel Procedures with CC and paid per admit up about $30K.
MO added +$0.8M and TN +$0.6M in similar acute hospital patterns; OH and NC add another +$0.6M largely from admission growth.
IN, MD, and TN show the same pressure in Family Care or ABD Non Dual acute hospital segments, indicating the pattern is recurring rather than isolated.

key_driver_codes: MAJ DEPRESS D/O SINGLE EPIS UNS
patterns_data.pattern_details: Inpatient behavioral health spend is increasing through a concentrated set of depression, psychosis, PTSD, and stress-related diagnoses rather than a broad-based trend. NC and VA are the largest identified markets, GA is concentrated at RIDGEVIEW INSTITUTE MONROE, and a material share remains UNATTRIBUTED, limiting clear local ownership. This is a focused inpatient BH utilization and intensity issue that needs clinical and UM action together.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: A small set of behavioral health diagnoses is driving a large share of spend, so targeted clinical criteria and length-of-stay management can have outsized impact.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Run targeted inpatient behavioral health review on depression, psychoses, and stress-related admissions, pair it with UM review of admission criteria and length-of-stay management, and assign market ownership for the UNATTRIBUTED activity.
patterns_data.validation_reason: A material portion of the spend sits in UNATTRIBUTED, so market ownership should be resolved before market-specific action plans are finalized.
evidence_summary: NC IP BH rose +$1.2M, led by Neuroses Except Depressive with +30 admissions for adjustment disorder and +11 admissions for PTSD.
UNATTRIBUTED IP BH adds about +$1.4M, centered on Psychoses and Depressive Neuroses, which limits clear market ownership until attribution is resolved.
VA contributes +$0.8M, mostly major depressive disorder and depression unspecified.
GA adds about +$0.7M, concentrated at RIDGEVIEW INSTITUTE MONROE across Psychoses and Depressive Neuroses diagnoses.

patterns_data.top_pattern: Acute psych admissions are a recurring Medicaid cost driver
patterns_data.pattern_details: Acute psych spend is rising across multiple Medicaid products and states, with both more admissions and higher paid per admit in the largest markets. CO and NC are the biggest drivers, while GA is heavily concentrated at RIDGEVIEW INSTITUTE MONROE. CO also has a sizable Not Mapped facility bucket, so part of the increase may reflect classification issues alongside real utilization and reimbursement pressure.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: This pattern combines real inpatient psychiatric use with possible facility classification issues, so it affects UM operations, provider economics, and data quality at the same time.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Audit acute psych admission appropriateness, authorization workflow, and rate exposure by product, starting with CO, NC, and GA, and correct CO facility classification records before taking broader pricing or policy action.
patterns_data.validation_reason: CO includes a material Not Mapped facility bucket, so some of the increase may reflect facility classification issues rather than pure utilization or reimbursement change.
evidence_summary: CO Family Care acute psych adds +$0.8M from +33 admissions, and another +$0.5M sits in Not Mapped facility records with paid per admit up about $19K.
NC TANF Foster Care acute psych rises +$0.8M with +28 admissions and paid per admit up about $29K.
GA acute psych adds about +$0.9M across TANF Standard and TANF Foster Care, heavily concentrated at RIDGEVIEW INSTITUTE MONROE.
NY and AR contribute another +$0.7M across ABD Non Dual, TANF Standard, and LTSS Non Dual acute psych stays.

patterns_data.top_pattern: Children's hospital spend is concentrated at two providers in IN and NY
patterns_data.pattern_details: Children's hospital spend is concentrated at two named providers and is being driven mainly by higher admission volume, not broad unit-cost inflation. IN is led by RILEY'S CHILDREN'S HEALTH, and NY is led by JOHN R. OISHEI CHILDRENS HOSPITAL. This creates a focused provider concentration issue where network, referral, and pediatric site-of-care levers are more relevant than across-the-board pricing changes.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: When spend growth is concentrated at a small number of children's hospitals, targeted provider and referral actions are more practical than broad product-wide interventions.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Review referral and admission patterns at RILEY'S CHILDREN'S HEALTH and JOHN R. OISHEI CHILDRENS HOSPITAL, and test whether some cases can be redirected or managed through lower-intensity pediatric settings when clinically appropriate.
evidence_summary: RILEY'S CHILDREN'S HEALTH in IN drives about +$1.0M across TANF Standard and Family Care children's admissions, including +86 admissions in the largest volume-led segment.
JOHN R. OISHEI CHILDRENS HOSPITAL in NY adds about +$0.7M across TANF Standard and CHIP Standard, with +89 admissions in the main TANF Standard segment.
In both states, spend growth is primarily volume-led while paid per admit is flat to down in the largest segments.

patterns_data.top_pattern: CA has a small number of very high-cost Med/Surg outlier cases
patterns_data.pattern_details: CA has a rare-case Med/Surg outlier pattern where a very small number of admissions account for a large share of spend. The biggest driver is anoxic brain damage, with extremely high cost per admit, alongside smaller clusters in alcoholic hepatitis and isolated high-cost bowel surgery cases. This is not a broad utilization trend; it is a case-level severity and payment exposure issue.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: A handful of catastrophic or rare admissions can distort trend and require different actions than routine utilization management.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Do case-level review of each outlier admission to confirm diagnosis severity, benefit coverage, stop-loss or outlier contract terms, and any need for one-time reserve or recovery action.
patterns_data.validation_reason: The pattern is flagged as low-volume, high-cost case-mix emergence with very small admission counts, so case-level confirmation is needed before broad action.
evidence_summary: CA rare IP Med/Surg cases add about +$1.1M from a very small number of admissions.
Two admissions for ANOXIC BRAIN DAMAGE NEC account for about +$0.5M, with paid per admit about $232K.
Alcoholic hepatitis with and without ascites add about +$0.3M across 15 admissions, and two single bowel surgery cases add another +$0.3M.

key_driver_codes: DVTRCLI LG INT NO PERF/ABSC W/O BL
patterns_data.pattern_details: Separate from the rare catastrophic cases, CA also has a broader recurring Med/Surg mix shift in liver disease and bowel surgery-related admissions. The main drivers are more admissions, with some diagnoses also showing higher paid per admit. This is a focused clinical pathway issue rather than a general inpatient trend across all Med/Surg care.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: Recurring liver and bowel surgery cases offer a more scalable clinical management opportunity than one-time outlier cases.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Target liver disease and bowel surgery pathways in CA for clinical management, including admission avoidance, complication management, and post-discharge planning for recurring cirrhosis and ostomy-related cases.
evidence_summary: CA broader IP Med/Surg case mix adds about +$0.9M outside the rare outlier cases.
ALCOHOLIC CIRRHOSIS LIVER W/ASCITES contributes +$0.3M with +25 admissions.
ENCOUNTER FOR ATTENTION ILEOSTOMY adds +$0.3M with +9 admissions and paid per admit up about $4K.
UNSPECIFIED CIRRHOSIS OF LIVER and diverticular bowel cases add another +$0.3M, pointing to a recurring liver and bowel surgery mix shift.
